thread:
mikhail: quick follow-up to the quant RFC — thinking out loud about a hierarchical routing + safety-net approach for mixed precision deployments. want a quick sanity check.

alix: curious, what's the core idea? tl;dr pls

mikhail: core: pick a preferred precision profile per-model (eg fp8-fast, int8-balanced, 4bit-cheap). at runtime, route requests to preferred variant, but have automated fallbacks: same-profile smaller batch on high-latency, fallback to int8 or fp8->int8 when quality drifts, and final fallback to full-precision if artifacting detected.

jamie: +1 on fallbacks. two immediate concerns: kv-cache compatibility across precisions, and kernel dispatch overhead when switching variants.

mikhail: good flags. kv-cache: propose per-request header that tags cache-precision-version; if mismatch, either re-encode cache on the fly (expensive) or invalidate local cache and fetch cold. aim to avoid silent corruption.

alix: re-encoding on the fly seems risky. can we instead keep short-lived warmed caches per-precision and prefer co-located routing? e.g., sticky routing for sessions.

jamie: sticky routing is doable. runtime change: maintain small per-GPU pools pinned to precision profiles to keep KV cache warm. adds fragmentation but reduces re-encode costs.

matthew: operational concern: how do we evaluate quality regressions that trigger fallbacks? simple perplexity delta won't cut it for chat + tool calls.

mikhail: plan: baseline metric set per workload: semantic similarity (embed-based), task-specific evals (e.g., instruction-following testset), plus latent token-level anomaly detector for hallucinations. fallback triggers are thresholded AND rolling-window check to avoid flapping.

sana: alerting here needs to be tight. a bad fallback loop could blow up latency budgets. propose two-level SLO guard: soft trigger that routes a small % to fallback for verification, hard trigger that flips traffic only after gated approval (automated or human).

alix: +1. also want a cheap canary harness: run a shadow path where candidate precision gets same input, compare outputs asynchronously to detect quality delta without impacting users.

mikhail: exactly. shadow compare + periodic offline full-eval on logged prompts (anonymized) to catch slow regressions.

jamie: implementation nit: kernel selection path should cache compiled kernels per (model,precision,seq_len) tuple. switching profiles should just pick cached kernel or fallback quickly; ensure we prewarm combos we expect to use in burst windows.

matthew: rollout/rollback UX: product wants per-customer pinning. we need consistent semantics: if customer pins to int8, don't auto-fallback except for emergency hard failures.

mikhail: agreed — customer pin overrides auto-routing. add policy precedence: customer pin > team config > auto routing.

sana: monitoring: emit these events: precision_switch_attempt, precision_switch_success, precision_fallback_reason, shadow_discrepancy_score. also add rate-limited alert on repeated switches.

alix: edge case: what about fine-tuned adapters or LoRA that are quantized differently? need compatibility matrix.

mikhail: good call. propose a simple compatibility table in model metadata: allowed-precisions + adapter-compat flags. loader will refuse incompatible combos and surface human-friendly error.

jamie: will the scheduler support heterogeneous batches (mixed precision within a batch) for latency efficiency? mixing in one batch is tricky for kernels.

mikhail: initial scope: no mixed-precision batching. schedule homogeneous batches, but allow interleaved small single-request fast-paths for low-latency. long-term: investigate mixed-kernel fusion but heavy engineering.

alix: can we define a compact policy DSL for precision profiles? examples: {name: "int8-balanced", quant: "int8", quality_thresholds: {...}, routes: {fallback: ["fp8","fp16"]}, sticky: true}

mikhail: yes — we'll spec a small JSON schema for profiles and surface in model registry UI. keep policies declarative.

matthew: one more: billing implications. we need to attribute tokens to precision profiles for cost analytics.

sana: agree — logs should include precision_label per request so billing + cost dashboards accurate.

ops-bot: deploy-check: integration tests for quant-routing harness passed on branch feature/quant-routing (CI 12m). :white_check_mark:

alix: next steps: draft a short RFC extension covering: compatibility table, kv-cache semantics, profile DSL, SLO guard flow, and rollout pin semantics. i'll take first pass.

mikhail: thanks — if you can drop a PR by EOD tomorrow i'll review. tagging @jamie for runtime bits and @sana for monitoring/alerts.

jamie: got it, will sketch kernel-caching and pool strategy.

sana: will outline alerting thresholds and emergency rollback hook.

mikhail: awesome. closing thread for now — we can spin smaller threads for each sub-area.
